payload.problem_domain: Heroes of Legend TTRPG rulebook chapter review and disposition

payload.statement:
Chapter under review: ch16 (quarto-book/chapters/16-armor-shields.qmd), "Armor & Shields", 130 lines.

Task: audit the chapter as a publishable unit and produce a disposition plan.
Each member audits through their own lens (see role card) and files a finding:
  stance support = the chapter holds on this lens as written
  stance refute  = the chapter must change; name the fix and its scope

Findings cite [file:line] in the chapter (16-armor-shields.qmd). Mechanics
findings state the broken value and the expected value. Cross-chapter checks
use the authoritative chapters as the reference, not this chapter (core
rules = ch06: DR math, minimum-1 damage, critical hit table, one-roll
principle; combat = ch13: Defense Roll tiers, cover, Defend maneuver,
actions/reactions; abilities = ch09: the printed Shield Block card;
disciplines = ch08: ladder and prereq table; bestiary = ch20: monster stat
blocks with DR; equipment = ch15: shield/armor pricing; skills roster =
ch07; starting kits and worked templates = ch02/ch05; glossary = ch21;
reference tables = ch22).

Disposition classes (for the librarian's synthesis):
  mechanical    - safe to implement as a micro-PR (headings, tables, wording,
                  em-dashes, single-cell refs, budget rows, worked-example
                  arithmetic that is canon-determined by another chapter)
  substantive   - needs a dispatched implementation pass (multi-file, new
                  content, worked-example rewrite requiring new narrative)
  design-decision - needs Bruce's ruling; implement the recommended default,
                  flagged veto-revertible in decisions-pending.md

Standing book conventions are in force: zero em-dashes in book text; damage
budgets flat at Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21; card costs 2/4/8;
Adept prereqs exactly 2, Master exactly 3; no flat +N damage riders anywhere
in the book (a damage bonus must be a budget row, a Basic-card floor of
1/2/3 + attribute, or a "+1 damage tier" bump); one-roll principle (the hit
or defense roll IS the outcome, no second damage roll); damage never drops
below 1 from any hit. Violations of these conventions are findings, not
questions.

Scope note: this chapter is the canonical home for armor and shield rules.
Where another chapter contradicts it, the finding should name BOTH files and
identify which is canonical (ch16 for armor/shield rules; ch06/ch13/ch20 for
core resolution, defense, and monster stat blocks). The council's output is
a disposition plan; it does not itself edit the book.

payload.argument: The chapter mostly holds (armor table, shield DR values, donning times, and the two Shield Block names in the glossary and combat chapter all match), but it fails as a publishable unit on five counts, which I organize by disposition. MECHANICAL: (1) the shield intro (lines 15, 68) states shields reduce damage only through a reaction, yet lines 70-74 grant passive shield DR that ch22's summary also lists; reword the intro. (2) Line 114 claims Roric takes nothing after Shield Block, but DR 7 vs incoming 5 leaves 1 HP by the minimum-1 floor. (3) Line 102's total of 7 mixes the chain mail table row (5) with the shield bonus (2) and needs a clarifying cross-reference to the shield section. (4) Line 59 promises a breastplate that carries no stealth penalty, contradicting its own table row (line 37) that grants none. (5) Line 122 steers players into a skill that exists in the ch07 roster but never gates donning or doffing in this chapter's rule text, so either the rule or the advice is missing. SUBSTANTIVE: (6) the Shield Block combat example (lines 100-114) presupposes a Critical damage tier and an additive critical bonus of 3, while ch06 makes three natural sixes an automatic Strong result plus a d6 effect table whose rows are not a flat addition; the passage must be rewritten around the real critical flow. (7) the tower shield's planted-cover maneuver (line 74) is a new reaction-style rule that the ch13 action economy, which lists only opportunity attack, shield block, and triggered abilities, never registers. DESIGN-DECISION: (8) ch09 prints a second Shield Block, a weapon maneuver card gated on 2 Armor with tier-scaled shield-DR additions (plus 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master plus 9 and 2 backlash), colliding in name and trigger with ch16's free tier-downgrade reaction; the glossary sides with ch16, so Bruce must rule whether the card is renamed, its effect merged into the reaction, or the reaction restricted to untrained users. INTERLOCKS: example (6) and the shield DR totals (4) and (7) all lean on values defined in other chapters (ch06 floor and critical table, ch13 cover tiers), so their fixes land in one coordinated pass; the card collision (8) gates whether the ch16 reaction keeps its current name in the glossary and reference sheet.

The armor section's total DR figure silently adds a shield bonus defined two sections later, an unmarked cross-reference inside a single example.

payload.argument: The chapter fails its own publishable-unit test under concrete player actions. First, the free reaction it grants every shield-bearer contradicts the ability canon: the disciplines chapter's prerequisite table and the printed card both list the block maneuver as an Adept purchase needing two Armor ranks, 4 DP, and a level-3 gate. As written here, a level-1 tank class whose starting kit already includes a standard shield gets the block on day one with zero investment, bypassing the ladder rule that higher tiers always require disciplines. The chapter must either declare the reaction gated by that card (naming the card and its prerequisites) or re-scope it as a universal basic defense; as published it hands out a purchased ability for free. Second, the worked example is arithmetically impossible. The bestiary stat block for a goblin carries 2/4/6 weapon damage, yet the scenario uses 3 on a middle-tier hit and 4 on a top-tier hit, and the three-sixes result is built from 4 base plus a bonus of 1 for a 7 total. No row of the critical table adds 1, and the maximum-damage row doubles the top tier (6 to 12); no combination of canon values yields 7. Worse, the example's step-down from a three-of-a-kind roll to the top tier is not one of the three transitions the rule line enumerates, and the core rules define such a roll as an automatic top-tier result plus a table bonus, so the tier-reduction wording has no defined target on a critical hit; the bonus die is never rolled or addressed, yet the text declares the bonus negated without any rule authorizing that. Third, stacking produces an uncapped wall: the chapter's own tables allow plate 6 plus tower shield 3 for 9 total, which pins every basic attack line (max 3, or 5 with the top Brawn modifier) and the entire goblin weapon line (max 6) at exactly 1 damage, forever, against a level-7 build; nothing in the chapter or the core rules caps or excludes such stacking, and the closing note's volume argument merely describes wearing the character down one point at a time rather than preventing the floor. Tested and holding: the tower shield's concealment numbers match the equipment chapter (both grant half cover to the bearer, and the larger cover value is a defined maneuver effect for an ally that the combat chapter's cover ladder recognizes), and the shield table's values match the reference sheet. Fixes required: gate the reaction to the card, rewrite the example with bestiary values and defined critical handling, and add an explicit cap or type restriction on stacked defensive values. Scope: substantive, multi-file.

Stacked values: plate 6 plus tower shield 3 equals 9 total; basic archery and thrown top out at 3, basic melee at 5 with a +2 Brawn modifier, and goblin weapons at 6, so every such attack lands for exactly 1 against that build, with no cap stated in the chapter or core rules.

payload.argument: Chapter 16 fails its own worked examples and collides with canon on four verified points. First, both examples use a goblin priced at 2/3/4 (Standard 3, Strong 4) while the ch20 bestiary stat block prices its scimitar at 2/4/6, so the broken values are Standard 3 -> 4 and Strong 4 -> 6; the block also arms the goblin with scimitar/shortbow, not the shortsword and crude spear the chapter puts in its hands. Second, the Shield Block scene invents a 'Critical' damage tier above Strong and a flat +3 critical bonus, but ch06 defines a critical as an automatic Strong result plus a d6 table effect (no numeric bonus exists); the scene then reports '5 (Strong only)' after the block when its own text priced Strong at 4, an internal arithmetic error on top of the off-canon framing. Third, Shield Block is written here as a universal reaction needing only a shield and a one-step tier drop, while ch09 prints it as a 2-Armor Adept weapon maneuver that reduces by shield DR plus 2/4/6, and ch08's prereq table corroborates the 2-Armor Adept gate; the two files cannot both hold, and the Level-1 example has Roric using the ability without buying the Adept card. Fourth, the scene has the DA rolling the goblins' attacks and a critical, which ch06's players-roll-all rule forbids (NPC outcomes derive from the player's Defense Roll). On the support side, the armor and shield tables match ch15 and ch22 exactly (DR, discipline requirements, Protection/PV values), the Protector template math (Brawn +2, Fortitude +1, Armor 1/2/4 Home cost) matches ch02/ch05/ch08, Endurance and Stealth exist in the ch07 roster, and the chapter carries no dangling section anchors. Fix scope: correct goblin values and weapon names (mechanical), rebuild critical arithmetic per ch06's d6 table (mechanical), rule which Shield Block implementation is canonical (design-decision), and rewrite the example around the player's Defense Roll (substantive).

payload.argument: Chapter 16 fails as a publishable unit on five mechanical fronts. (a) Name collision: the chapter's no-prereq Shield Block reaction (L78, tier-down-one-step) collides with ch09's printed Shield Block card (2 Armor, Adept gate, L373-385), the ch08 prereq row (L103), and the ch22 reaction list; ch21's glossary entry matches ch16's free version, so the name lands on two different mechanics. The canonical card is ch09's (ch08's table confirms the 2 Armor / Adept gate); ch16's block must be renamed or re-gated. ch09's flat 'shield DR + 2/4/6/9/12' rider breaks the zero-flat-rider law (legal shapes are a budget row, a 1/2/3 + attribute floor, or a +1 damage tier bump) and should be rebuilt as a 1/2/3 + Fortitude floor. L0 availability is unsound: a level-1 tank with a kit shield gets the reaction free, while ch09 gates it at Adept (level 3). (b) Armor table: prereq shapes (1 Armor = Novice, 2 Armor = Adept, 3 Armor = Master) match ch08 exactly; the spellcasting-penalty column (none / -1 / -1 / -2 / -3) has no cross-chapter conflict, since ch10 forbids spell-failure mechanics and no other chapter imposes armor casting costs. (c) Shield table: Buckler/Shield 1 Protection and Tower 2 Protection match ch15 L93, and Protection is a real Defense discipline (ch08 L43); but ch16 treats Protection as an armor-style prereq shape while ch22 L303 defines PV as a stance bonus from Bastion or Arcane Shield, and ch05's Bastion gives +1 PV, so the two PV semantics must be reconciled. (d) Worked example, against the ch20 goblin (scimitar 2/4/6, DR 0) and ch06: 'Standard hit, 3 damage' should be 4; 'Strong hit, 4 damage' should be 6; the crit line, which stacks an invented flat bonus on the Strong hit to reach 7, should be 12, because the ch06 critical table has no flat-damage bonus row and its row 1 (Maximum Damage) doubles the Strong value (6+6); 'Damage is now 5 (Strong only)' should be 6; 'Roric takes 7 damage' should be 12; and 'he takes nothing' should be 1, contradicting ch16 L112's own 'soaks all but 1' and the min-1 rule (ch06 L69, ch16 L80). (e) Tower shield: the -5 ft carry penalty double-counts, since ch02 L538's 20 ft already folds the heavy-armor -5 in; the plant-for-three-quarters-ally claim (L74) collides with ch13's cover table (L330-334) and with cover being a Defense-roll modifier (ch13 L124), while ch22 L303 grants the tower shield only passive half cover; 'Shield: 1 action' (L120) collides with ch13 L360, where a buckler is drawn as a free action. The 1/5/10-minute donning ladder and the Endurance skill cite (ch07 L110) are internally consistent and sound.

The level-1 dwarf Protector template carries chain mail plus shield for 7 total DR and 13 hit points (10 + Fort 1 + Know 0 + Sturdy 2), the same kit the example gives Roric, so the corrected 12-damage crit leaves him at 1 HP.

The cover table sets half cover at -1 and three-quarters at -3 to the attacker, and a buckler can be drawn as a free action, colliding with ch16's one-action shield donning and the planted-ally cover claim.

payload.argument: One name carries two mechanics: ch16's Shield Block is a free tier-stepping reaction for any shield-wielder, while ch09's printed Shield Block card is a 2-Armor Adept purchase that reduces damage by shield DR plus a tiered bonus, and ch08's prereq table matches the card while ch21's glossary matches ch16 — so the book contradicts itself on trigger, effect, and access, and ch16's Level-1 Roric uses the reaction without the card's Adept gate. The goblin vignettes arm goblins with a shortsword and a crude spear the bestiary's goblin (scimitar/shortbow) never carries, and the chapter's own examples disagree on Roric's gear: he buys Breastplate + Shield, then fights in Chain Mail + Shield. Voice, however, holds: Roric's protector characterization, the DA Guidance box, and the closing callout all match the fiction and ch13 registers; the main fix is renaming or harmonizing the reaction with the card, and aligning the goblin weapons to the stat block.

payload.argument: As a publishable unit this chapter is incomplete, and the gaps are structural rather than cosmetic. First, the shield's Protection value is a dead stat: every shield row lists a Protection number plus a DR bonus, but the chapter never states what the Protection number does for a shield-bearer at the table, and the Defense Roll modifier list elsewhere has no Protection entry. A player cannot tell whether their shield's Protection value is a prerequisite, a defensive bonus, or flavor, so they will stall. Second, the chapter makes no statement at all about how armor or shields interact with the Defend maneuver or with PV sources like Bastion or Arcane Shield; those are the two named PV generators and the chapter that owns shields is silent on the interaction. Third, the Shield Block worked example teaches a Critical-to-Strong downgrade that the Shield Block rule text never defines; the rule lists only the Strong, Standard, and Weak steps, so the example contradicts the rule as written. Fourth, the chapter has zero outgoing cross-references, so a reader landing here is not routed to the reaction economy, the discipline rules, the Shield Block ability card, or the pricing chapter; meanwhile the reference chapter duplicates the armor and shield tables without ever pointing back to this canonical home, creating drift risk. Fifth, no armor or shield carries a price anywhere, so the chapter does not let a player buy what it describes. Fix scope: add a short Protection/PV definition paragraph in the Shields section, one sentence on Defend and PV-source interaction, a Critical line to the Shield Block rule, an outgoing cross-reference list, and a price column; the Shield Block example then follows the corrected rule.

evidence.claim: Each shield row pairs a Protection value with a DR bonus, yet the chapter never defines what the Protection value does at the table, leaving it a dead stat.
The Defense Roll modifier list has no Protection or PV entry, so the shield's Protection value has no defined effect in the combat resolution chapter.
The reference chapter's shield table adds a Protection Value column and a defense summary, but it never points back to this chapter as the canonical home for the full rules.

The Shield Block worked example downgrades a critical to Strong and negates the critical bonus, a step the rule text never defines, so the example teaches a rule that is not written.

evidence.claim: Bastion and Arcane Shield are the two named sources that raise Protection Value, yet the chapter that owns shields never states how that value interacts with armor or shields in play.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Add +1 to your Protection Value for the round

The chapter contains no outgoing cross-reference at all, so a reader landing mid-chapter is not routed to the reaction economy, discipline rules, the Shield Block ability card, or the pricing chapter.

payload.argument: As a page-rendering unit, ch16 is broadly clean: heading levels match sibling rule chapters, both tables lay out with no column overflow, header rows, or unbalanced cells, the em-dash ban is honored (zero in source), callouts and the DA Guidance blockquote mirror ch13/ch15, and pagebreaks sit where siblings place them. But the chapter-opening figure is the one real layout defect, and it is confirmed in the built PDF, not just in the markdown. The image line carries the art number inside its caption text, and the same number plus the word 'illustration' is then repeated in a hand-written italic line directly below. On the rendered page the auto figure label and the manual caption therefore stack into a doubled caption (the number 23 and 'illustration' each appear twice on the opening spread). This is not unique to ch16: I verified all 21 chapter-opening figures in the build exhibit the same doubled pattern, so the fix is a book-wide caption convention decision (drop the hand-written line, or strip the number from the alt text), not a ch16-only edit. I also note the brief's table description (six rows, Speed and Armor Req columns) does not match the chapter's actual table (eight armor rows, Discipline and Notes columns); the real table is correctly formed and needs no change. Scope: the doubled opening-figure caption is a book-wide mechanical fix (wording/caption, single pattern repeated per chapter); the rest of the layout holds.

evidence.claim: The opening image line embeds the art number in its caption text, which the renderer then prefixes with an auto figure label, producing a redundant double caption.
A second hand-written italic caption line repeats the same number and the word illustration immediately under the image, doubling the caption on the page.
The armor table is five columns (name, discipline, DR, stealth, notes) with eight data rows, not the six-row Speed/Armor-Req table the brief describes; it is correctly formed.
The source contains no em-dash or en-dash characters, so the chapter complies with the book's zero-em-dash rule.
Every one of the 21 chapter-opening figures in the built PDF shows the same doubled caption, so this is a book-wide convention, not a defect isolated to ch16.
The DA Guidance note is a blockquote with a bold lead-in, the identical form used by the combat and GM chapters.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: > **DA Guidance:** Let the player declare Shield Block

payload.rationale: t-01 closed rejected 7-0 with zero rebuttals (reject quorum 4 exceeded; all 7 findings un-rebutted, unanimous refute). Every lens independently found the Shield Block name collision (f-001/002/003/004/005/006); f-004 notes the canonical majority (ch20 Knight, ch21 glossary, ch22 reaction list) all match ch16's free reaction, and the ch09 card additionally violates the flat-rider law (shield DR + 2/4/6/9/12 is not a legal damage shape). The goblin damage error is verified against ch20's 2/4/6 scimitar (f-003). The Critical-4-plus-3-equals-7 arithmetic matches no ch06 critical row (f-002/003/004). The DA-rolls framing contradicts ch06/ch13's players-roll-all rule (f-003). 'Takes nothing' violates the chapter's own minimum-1 floor (f-001/002). The ch15 armor table confirms armor has no price column (f-006 pricing finding stands; ch15's armor table has no Cost column while the weapons table does). The ch22 shield table's 'PV' column is actually the Protection discipline requirement, and ch21's PV glossary entry wrongly names shields as a PV source (f-004/006). The doubled opening-figure caption is confirmed book-wide across all 21 chapters (f-007) and is routed to decisions-pending, not fixed per-chapter. The breastplate-callout item in f-001 was re-verified against the table and is consistent (no fix); the tower-shield plant maneuver is a maneuver using ch13's defined cover vocabulary (half/three-quarters cover), so it is consistent with the action economy (no fix needed, add cross-ref only).
payload.recommendation: Chapter 16 (Armor & Shields) is REJECTED as a publishable unit: the Shield Block reaction it grants to every shield-wielder collides with the printed 2-Armor Adept Shield Block card in ch09 (and ch08's prereq example row), the two worked examples use goblin damage values (Standard 3 / Strong 4) that contradict the ch20 bestiary (2/4/6) and invent a Critical damage tier plus a flat +3 critical bonus that ch06's critical rules do not contain, the combat example has the DA rolling attacks (contradicting the players-roll defense model in ch06/ch13) and ends with Roric taking zero damage (violating the minimum-1 rule), the armor-choice example's gear contradicts the combat example's gear, the PV/Protection vocabulary is ambiguous across ch16/ch21/ch22, and the chapter lacks pricing and outgoing cross-references. Fix per disposition plan: one ch16 rewrite pass (worked examples, shield intro wording, protection prereq clarity, cross-refs), the ch09 card removed to end the name collision (ch08 row swapped), ch06/ch21/ch22 vocabulary and number cross-fixes, and the doubled-figure-caption convention routed to decisions-pending as book-wide.

resolved.outcome: rejected (7-0 unanimous refute, no rebuttals, no impasse, no judge)
